description: Hard synthetic retrieval cases designed to expose lexical failure modes and test semantic retrieval. Labels are benchmark annotations only, not official NRIF decisions.
design_goals: lexically tempting but semantically wrong candidates

cases.query: early detection of crop infections from leaf photographs using artificial intelligence

candidates.text: Computer vision can identify plant pathogens from farmer-captured foliage images before visible damage becomes widespread.
Machine learning models classify maize leaf disease using annotated images collected from experimental plots.
Digital photography is used to document crop growth stages and fertilizer response in field trials.
Artificial intelligence predicts seasonal harvest volumes from historical agricultural production statistics.
A mobile platform sends agricultural extension messages and collects farmer survey responses.

cases.query: predict maternal complications and route high-risk women to appropriate care

candidates.text: A clinical risk engine identifies women requiring escalation and supports referral from community providers to facilities.
Maternal health education materials are distributed through community health workers and mobile phones.
A hospital dashboard tracks antenatal attendance, deliveries and postnatal follow-up.
Machine learning forecasts outpatient clinic workload from historical appointment records.
A referral directory lists nearby maternity facilities, ambulance contacts and opening hours.

cases.query: detect unusual contamination patterns in drinking water sensor streams

candidates.text: Streaming measurements from water-quality probes are analysed to flag abnormal chemical and microbial signatures.
Water monitoring stations report pH, turbidity and temperature at regular intervals.
Anomaly detection identifies unusual electricity consumption in municipal pumping stations.
Community teams test drinking-water samples manually using field kits.
A dashboard visualizes environmental sensor readings and maintenance alerts.

cases.query: estimate photovoltaic generation from meteorological observations

candidates.text: A time-series model forecasts solar farm output using irradiance, cloud cover, temperature and wind measurements.
Weather observations are used to issue drought advisories for smallholder farmers.
Solar mini-grid feasibility is assessed using household demand and geographic access data.
Machine learning estimates electricity demand from historical smart-meter records.
Photovoltaic panels are monitored for faults and maintenance requirements.

cases.query: match researchers across records despite different spellings and initials

candidates.text: Entity resolution links Dr. A. Mukamana with Alice Mukamana across repository and grant records.
Author disambiguation connects Jean Claude Niyonzima, J.C. Niyonzima and J. Niyonzima using institutional affiliations.
Author names are exported exactly as entered by applicants without normalization.
Researcher profiles contain ORCID identifiers and publication lists.
Duplicate publications are detected when DOI values are identical.

cases.query: find proposals addressing the same scientific objective even when wording differs

candidates.text: The study develops an automated method for recognizing crop pathogens from images of symptomatic leaves.
Researchers propose computer-assisted diagnosis of plant disease using photographs captured in farming communities.
The project trains farmers to recognize common crop diseases by visual inspection.
The team builds a database of agricultural photographs for extension training.
The project studies fertilizer application effects on maize yield.

cases.query: identify a publication missing from the national repository

candidates.text: International index record: Niyonzima JC. Community-based maternal referral pathways in rural Rwanda. 2025. DOI 10.1234/example.5678.
National repository record: Niyonzima J.C. Community health worker training for maternal services. 2025.
Repository contains a 2024 article by Niyonzima on rural maternal health access.
DOI registry record for a paper about community referral systems in East Africa, 2023.
National repository metadata export containing all records deposited during 2025.

cases.query: separate a genuinely duplicate application from another proposal in the same research area

candidates.text: This application repeats the same intervention, population, study design and expected outcomes as the earlier submitted proposal, with only minor wording changes.
A separate study evaluates a different crop disease intervention in the same agricultural region.
Another proposal uses the same machine learning technique but studies livestock rather than crops.
A related project uses agricultural images for farmer training, not disease diagnosis.
A previous application concerns crop disease surveillance but proposes a different target population and field design.

cases.query: retrieve evidence about whether ethics approval is present

candidates.text: The protocol states that approval was obtained from the institutional research ethics committee before participant recruitment began.
The proposal describes informed consent procedures and plans to submit the protocol for review.
The research team lists its institutional affiliations and previous ethics training.
The project includes a data protection plan for storing participant information.
The applicant requests budget support for regulatory and compliance activities.

cases.query: locate evidence that the requested budget stays below the funding ceiling

candidates.text: The total amount requested is RWF 48,500,000, which is below the programme maximum of RWF 50,000,000.
The financial plan allocates funds to personnel, equipment, travel and field activities.
The proposal requests additional co-financing from an institutional partner.
The programme guidelines describe eligible expenditure categories and reporting requirements.
The budget narrative explains the cost of data collection and laboratory analysis.
